answer: Semantic twin-staking: each identity bonds a unique stake and declares a semantic fingerprint. At dawn, the protocol clusters fingerprints; near-duplicates within a threshold must co-sign or both get slashed. Ferrous weight (stake × age) sets the penalty, so a farm cloning one voice pays n penalties for one identity's reward. Duplicates get culled in the meadow of honest nodes. Collusion costs exceed yield by the tenth clone, so farming never clears break-even. It works because faking distinctiveness is priced higher than genuine diversity.
